text:
sanjay: Heads-up — noticed p95 p99 jitter in dedicated-pool-usw1 around 02:43. small-token chat gen latency spiking ~120ms -> 300ms. pattern correlates with egress bursts on TORs. anyone watching nets?
elaine: looking. which racks and any noisy tenants?
sanjay: r20/r21. quick tail of net counters: 
```
2026-03-02T02:43:12Z tor-agent[tor-3]: tx_bytes tenant=tenant-77 delta=85MB/s
2026-03-02T02:43:15Z shard-proxy[proxy-11]: conn_open tenant=tenant-90 prefill=true prefills=3
2026-03-02T02:43:18Z scheduler[svc]: alloc-frag tenant=tenant-90 reason=warmup-crossrack
```
sanjay: tenant-77 is doing a steady KV backup pattern; tenant-90 is doing aggressive cross-rack warmups (recent fractional promotion). combined they're saturating tor uplink and triggering slab fragmentation.
cory: ok that matches the infra alert. billing-bot flagged a surprise egress invoice for one org — ops wants immediate throttle.
oncall-sre: i'm oncall. short mitigation plan: 1) soft-isolate tenant-90 into a no-prefill group for 30m, 2) apply per-tenant egress cap 50MB/s on pool-proxy for risky pools, 3) reduce allocator prefill parallelism to 1. can someone run the commands?
ops-automation: commands ready: 
```bash
# move tenant-90 to no-prefill group
rctl tenant update tenant-90 --policy=no-prefill --note="temp isolation for egress surge"
# leash egress for dedicated pool
rctl config set prod pool-proxy egress_leash_per_tenant=true
rctl config set prod pool-proxy egress_leash_bytes_per_sec=52428800
# slow prefill concurrency
rctl config set prod allocator prefill_concurrency_limit=1
```
elaine: before we change, can we confirm tenant-90 is the warmup culprit? quick query: 
```sql
SELECT tenant, sum(tx_bytes) as tx FROM net.tor_stats WHERE time > now() - 15m GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY tx DESC LIMIT 6;
```
elaine: ran it — tenant-90 and tenant-77 top two. tenant-90 shows many short-lived connections flagged prefill=true.
sanjay: ok do the changes. also add a temp iptables rule to slow bulk KV backups from tenant-77 while billing is investigated?
ops-automation: applied both: tenant-90 policy changed, egress leash and prefill_concurrency applied. infra-bot: config change recorded user=oncall-sre action=set pool-proxy.egress_leash_per_tenant=true at=2026-03-02T02:50:04Z
oncall-sre: monitoring now. please keep an eye on p99 and tor tx.
cory: watching dashboards — within 60s p99 dropped from 310ms to 130ms. tor tx for tenant-90 fell to ~6MB/s. tenant-77 still at ~40MB/s but less bursty.
billing-bot: provisional charge retained for org until postmortem completed. estimated excess egress ~0.8TB -> ~$720. ops wants root cause and guardrail proposal.
elaine: immediate follow-ups: 1) add alert for sustained per-tenant egress > 60MB/s over 5m in dedicated pools, 2) make no-prefill policy an option in tenant promotion flow with safety check, 3) add migration checklist step to validate rack headroom pre-warm. i'll file tickets.
sanjay: medium-term: scheduler should avoid cross-rack warmups when TOR utilization > 70% and prefer local warmups or paced prefetch. also consider adding a cheap TOR headroom probe before starting multi-rack prefill.
oncall-sre: agree. also request adding an automated rollback for promotions that trigger immediate egress surge alert within 10m.
cory: i'll draft a short postmortem note and include the commands we ran + cost numbers. link to draft PR: https://git.redwood/postmortems/infra/2026-03-02-egress-surge.md
ops-automation: note: we can set default egress leash to false in templates but add a promotion-time toggle. config path: /configs/tenants/promotion.json -> field `allow_crossrack_prefill` default=false for fractional promotions.
elaine: PRs for alerts and promotion flow incoming. assign to infra-scheduler and allocator owners.
sanjay: thanks all. feel free to @oncall-sre here if it flares back. closing loop unless anyone sees recurrence. :thumbsup:
